objective.text: Use sticky read routing after a write without claiming replication is synchronous.

difficulty.rationale: Understand connection routing without assuming replication has caught up.

runtime.sapi: Isolated CLI Laravel harness unless another context is explicitly stated
runtime.errorPolicy: E_ALL; UTC; no external services or application data

stem: A request uses a configured read/write connection with sticky=true. After a successful write on that connection, where do subsequent ordinary reads go during that request?

options.text: To the replica after Laravel waits for a matching replication position.
options.rationale: The sticky option does not implement a replica catch-up wait protocol.
options.misconception: The sticky option does not implement a replica catch-up wait protocol.

options.text: To whichever connection returned the first read result, even after the write.
options.rationale: The post-write modification state changes routing; it is not fixed by the first read.
options.misconception: The post-write modification state changes routing; it is not fixed by the first read.

options.text: To the write connection; this gives read-after-write visibility without making replication synchronous.
options.rationale: The modified-record flag and sticky option route reads to the writer for the current connection lifecycle.

options.text: To the replica as usual because stickiness affects writes only.
options.rationale: The purpose of sticky routing is to redirect later reads after a write.
options.misconception: The purpose of sticky routing is to redirect later reads after a write.
